## Model Performance Summary: Categories

### Our Current Models - LOCALLY RUN (FREE)

From the active setup (LiteLLM :4000 routing, vLLM :8000, Ollama :11434):

- **Qwen2.5-14B** (vLLM on port 8000): ~8,192 total context. Local GPU inference (desktop RTX 5070 12GB VRAM). Suitable for coding, basic agents, file reading. TPS: not recently measured in shared data; typically 30-60+ on 12GB cards for similar sizes with good quantization.
- **Ollama-managed models** (port 11434): Various local/cloud hybrids. Current local focus appears limited; hardware supports more.

**Hardware context (from user profile + research):**
- Desktop: Intel i9-14900K + RTX 5070 (12GB VRAM). Best for 7-14B dense or efficient MoE at high relative speed.
- ASUS GX10 (GB10 Grace Blackwell, 128GB unified LPDDR5X, ~1 PFLOP FP4, storage 1-4TB NVMe): Excellent for 30B-120B+ MoE/quantized models. Multiple concurrent instances possible. Storage is not a limiter for several large models (20-80GB each).
- Laptops (Legion Pro 5, ThinkPad X1 Yoga, Yoga Book 9i, Acer Chromebook): Secondary; Chromebook limited; others can run smaller models or remote to GX10/desktop.

**Are there more performance-efficient local free models?** Yes.

**GX10 recommendations (local free, high efficiency):**
- **Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (NVFP4/Q4)**: ~90-110+ tok/s single-stream (measured on real GX10/vLLM with MTP), 262K context. Strong coding, reasoning, agents, vision/video support in family. Concurrent scaling excellent (hundreds aggregate). Fits with headroom for other models/ComfyUI. ~20-40GB quantized.
- **gpt-oss-120b (MXFP4)**: ~45 tok/s decode-heavy (StorageReview/vLLM on GX10), larger knowledge, 131K+ context. Fits in 128GB.
- **Qwen3.8-27B / Qwen3 Coder variants (NVFP4)**: High quality coding, ~30-60+ tok/s, 128K-256K context. Multiple instances possible.
- **Nemotron 3.5 / Nano variants (quantized)**: NVIDIA-optimized, good on GB10. Check Hugging Face GGUF/NVFP4.
- Smaller: Gemma 4 12B/26B-A4B, Qwen3.5 9B for speed/low VRAM if needed alongside.

**Desktop RTX 5070 (12GB) recommendations:**
- Qwen3.5 9B (Q6_K): ~60 tok/s, good all-rounder.
- Gemma 4 12B (Q4/Q8): Multimodal (text/image/audio), long context efficiency.
- Phi-4 or similar 14B Q3/Q4: High speed (~70 tok/s).
- Avoid large dense; use MoE with offload if needed (slower).

**Local free advantages:** Privacy, no rate limits, zero token cost, offline. Capabilities: coding, file reading, agents (with tools), vision (multimodal models), web via external tools. Context limited by VRAM/KV cache (8K-256K practical).

**Storage note:** GX10 1-4TB easily holds 5-10 large models + data. Desktop/laptop more constrained by VRAM than disk.

### Our Current Models - FREE (CLOUD)

- **free-HighTPS_Context** alias (LiteLLM): Rotates **Nemotron 3.5 Lightning :free** (30B total / 3B active, text-only, ~52 measured e2e TPS short calls, 1M advertised context) and **Nemotron 3.5 Super-VL :free** (120B / 12B active, multimodal text+image+video, ~20 TPS, 1M context). Zero-price OpenRouter endpoints, 240s timeout, no paid fallback. Picker: 900K input + 8K output. Large-context test: both retained facts at ~779K tokens; Super-VL better at JSON formatting.

**Better free cloud options?**
- **Groq free tier**: Qwen3.8-27B, gpt-oss-120b/20b. Advertised 450-1000+ tok/s (LPU), measured high (e.g. ~0.4s median latency). Context ~131K. Rate limits: ~30 RPM, 1K RPD, 8K TPM, 200K TPD. No card needed. Excellent for high-TPS agent/coding bursts.
- **Cerebras**: Similar high speed (wafer-scale, 2000+ tok/s advertised) on gpt-oss-120b / Qwen3.8-27B; $5 trial credit, card often required, limited context on free.
- Other OpenRouter free (as of Nov 11 2026): Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-A55B:free (1M, frontier reasoning but slower ~29 TPS), Gemma 4 26B/31B:free (vision, 262K), Cohere North Mini Code:free (coding, no training on prompts), Inkling 2 Small:free (1M, vision), ERNIE-5.5-Flash:free (1M), etc. Super-VL remains top for reliability + multimodal + 1M in independent tests (20/20 pass rates).
- Google Gemini free tier: Flash/Flash-Lite models, generous limits, strong capabilities, but content may train models.

**Free cloud strengths:** High context (1M on Nemotron), multimodal, zero cost, easy API. Weaknesses: rate limits, potential prompt retention/training, variable uptime, not private.

### Our Current Models - PAID (CLOUD)

From recent short-call benchmarks (completion tokens / wall time, 2 calls each; not sustained decode):

| Model                  | Measured mean TPS | Advertised context | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------------|--------------------|-------|
| FREE Lightning        | 52               | 1,000,000         | Text, fast agent |
| FREE Super-VL         | 20               | 1,000,000         | Multimodal |
| Paid Mercury-3 (Inception) | 548            | 1,000,000         | ~10.6× faster than Lightning |
| Paid Grok 4.7         | 99               | 500,000           | ~1.9× Lightning |
| Paid DeepSeek V4 Pro  | 62               | 1,048,576         | Reasoning consumed budget |
| Paid Kimi K3.1 Pro    | 34               | 1,048,576         | Same; temp=1 required |

**More efficient paid options?**
- Mercury-3 stands out for pure speed + 1M context.
- Groq/Cerebras paid tiers for extreme TPS on open models (often cheaper than frontier).
- DeepSeek/Kimi good for large context but lower useful TPS if reasoning-heavy.
- Consider Google Gemini 2.5/3.x Flash (high speed, multimodal, competitive pricing), Claude Haiku variants, or xAI Grok upgrades if available.
- Providers like DeepInfra, Together, Nebius often have lower prices on open weights.
